dhpak1.7:1.1: 1.6 The Story about Culla Kāḷa and Mahā Kāḷa Cullakāḷa-Mahākāḷavatthu
dhpak1.7:2.2: [28.184] this Dhamma teaching was given by the Teacher while he was in residence near the city Setavya with reference to Culla Kāḷa and Mahā Kāḷa.
dhpak1.7:3.1: For Culla Kāḷa, Majjhima Kāḷa, and Mahā Kāḷa were three householders who lived in Setavya, and they were brothers.
dhpak1.7:3.2: The oldest and youngest used to travel abroad with their caravan of five hundred carts and bring home goods to sell,
dhpak1.7:3.3: and Majjhima Kāḷa sold the goods they brought.
dhpak1.7:3.4: Now on a certain occasion the two {1.67} brothers, taking wares of various kinds in their five hundred carts,
dhpak1.7:3.5: set out for Sāvatthī, and halting between Sāvatthī and Jetavana, unharnessed their carts.
dhpak1.7:4.1: At eventide Mahā Kāḷa saw noble disciples, residents of Sāvatthī, with garlands and perfumes in their hands, going to hear the Dhamma.
dhpak1.7:4.2: “Where are they going?” he asked. Receiving the answer that they were going to listen to the Dhamma, he thought to himself: “I will go too.”
dhpak1.7:4.3: So he addressed his youngest brother:
dhpak1.7:4.4: “Dear brother, keep watch over the carts; I am going to listen to the Dhamma.”
dhpak1.7:4.5: So saying, he went and worshipped the Realised One and sat down in the outer circle of the assembly.
dhpak1.7:5.1: On that day the Teacher taught the Dhamma in orderly sequence with reference to Mahā Kāḷa’s disposition of mind,
dhpak1.7:5.2: and quoting the Discourse on the Aggregates of Suffering, and other discourses,
dhpak1.7:5.3: discoursed on the dangers, degradation and defilements of sensual pleasures.
dhpak1.7:5.4: Mahā Kāḷa, after listening to the discourse, thought to himself: “So a man must leave all things behind him when he goes hence.
dhpak1.7:5.5: When a man goes to the world beyond, neither wealth nor kinsmen can follow him.
dhpak1.7:5.6: Why should I continue to live the life of a householder? I will go forth.”
dhpak1.7:5.7: Accordingly, when the multitude had worshipped the Teacher and departed, he requested the Teacher to give him the going forth.
dhpak1.7:6.1: “Have you no kinsman of whom it is proper that you should ask permission?” enquired the Teacher.
dhpak1.7:6.2: “I have a younger brother, venerable Sir.” – “Ask his permission.” – “Very well, venerable Sir.”
dhpak1.7:6.3: So Mahā Kāḷa went to Culla Kāḷa and said to him: “Dear brother, [28.185] receive all this wealth.”
dhpak1.7:6.4: {1.68} – “But you, brother?” – “I intend to go forth under the Teacher.”
dhpak1.7:6.5: Culla Kāḷa used all manner of arguments to dissuade his brother from carrying out his intention, but in vain.
dhpak1.7:6.6: Finally he said to him: “Very well, master; do as you wish.”
dhpak1.7:6.7: So Mahā Kāḷa went forth under the Teacher. Culla Kāḷa likewise went forth.
dhpak1.7:6.8: But the thought in Culla Kāḷa’s mind was: “After a time I will return to the world and take my brother with me.”
dhpak1.7:7.1: Somewhat later Mahā Kāḷa took higher ordination, and approaching the Teacher, asked him:
dhpak1.7:7.2: “How many duties are there in this dispensation?”
dhpak1.7:7.3: The Teacher informed him that there were two.
dhpak1.7:7.4: Mahā Kāḷa said: “Venerable Sir, since I went forth in old age, I shall not be able to fulfill the duty of study, but I can fulfill the duty of meditation.”
dhpak1.7:7.5: So he had the Teacher instruct him in the ascetic practice of living in a charnel ground, which leads to Arahatship.
dhpak1.7:7.6: At the end of the first watch, when everyone else was asleep, he went to the charnel ground;
dhpak1.7:7.7: and at dawn, before anyone else had risen, he returned to the monastery.
dhpak1.7:8.1: The Charnel Ground Now the keeper of the charnel ground, a certain woman named Kāḷī,
dhpak1.7:8.2: whose duty was to burn the bodies of the dead, saw the elder as he stood up and sat down and walked about.
dhpak1.7:8.3: And she thought to herself: “Who can this be that comes here? I will find out about him.”
dhpak1.7:8.4: But she was unable to find out what she wished to find out about him.
dhpak1.7:8.5: So one night she lighted a lamp in the hut of the charnel ground, and taking son and daughter with her, hid herself on one side of the charnel ground.
dhpak1.7:8.6: When she saw the elder approach, she approached him, worshipped him, and asked him: “Venerable Sir, does our noble bhikkhu reside in this place?”
dhpak1.7:8.7: – “Yes, lay sister.” – “Venerable Sir, {1.69} those that reside in a charnel ground have certain rules to observe.”
dhpak1.7:8.8: The elder did not say: “Do you think I shall observe any rules of your telling?”
dhpak1.7:8.9: Instead he said: “What ought I to do, lay sister?”
dhpak1.7:9.1: Said the keeper of the charnel ground:
dhpak1.7:9.2: “Venerable Sir, they that reside in a charnel ground are bound to declare the fact to the keepers of the charnel ground,
dhpak1.7:9.3: to the chief elder at the monastery, and to the village headman.” – “Why?”
dhpak1.7:9.4: – “Thieves who commit depredations, when pursued by lawful owners of property, frequently flee to a charnel ground and leave their spoils there;
dhpak1.7:9.5: then the owners come and threaten residents of the charnel ground with harm.
dhpak1.7:9.6: But if the authorities are duly informed, they can avert trouble by saying:
dhpak1.7:9.7: [28.186] ‘We know for a fact that this venerable bhikkhu has resided here for such and such a length of time; he is no thief.’
dhpak1.7:9.8: For this reason you are bound to declare your intention to the authorities I have mentioned.”
dhpak1.7:10.1: Mahā Kāḷa then asked: “Is there anything else I ought to do?”
dhpak1.7:10.2: – “Venerable Sir, so long as your reverence resides in a charnel ground, you must abstain from fish, flesh, sesame, flour, oil, and molasses.
dhpak1.7:10.3: You must not sleep by day. You must not be slothful.
dhpak1.7:10.4: You must live with high resolve, exerting all the powers of your will, avoiding double-dealing and deceit.
dhpak1.7:10.5: At eventide, when all are asleep, you must leave the monastery and come here; at dawn, before any have risen, you must return to the monastery.
dhpak1.7:10.6: In case, venerable Sir, while you reside in this charnel ground, you succeed in reaching the goal of the spiritual life,
dhpak1.7:10.7: and they bring a dead body here and cast it away, I will place it on the funeral pyre,
dhpak1.7:10.8: and rendering the usual honors with perfumes and garlands, I will perform the funeral rites over the body.
dhpak1.7:10.9: If you do not succeed, I will light the pyre, drag the body along with a stake,
dhpak1.7:10.10: {1.70} throw it outside, chop it to pieces with an axe, throw the pieces into the fire, and burn it.”
dhpak1.7:10.11: The elder said to her: “Very well, woman.
dhpak1.7:10.12: But in case you should see a corpse which you think would afford me a suitable subject of meditation on material form, be good enough to tell me.”
dhpak1.7:10.13: – “Very well,” said she, promising him to do so.
dhpak1.7:11.1: In accordance with his intention the Elder Mahā Kāḷa performed his meditations in the charnel ground.
dhpak1.7:11.2: The Elder Culla Kāḷa, however, busy and active, thinking always of the household life, remembering son and wife, said to himself:
dhpak1.7:11.3: “It is an excessively difficult task my brother is engaged in.”
dhpak1.7:12.1: Now a certain young woman of station was attacked by a disease, and the very moment the disease attacked her,
dhpak1.7:12.2: she died, at eventide, without a sign of withering or weariness.
dhpak1.7:12.3: In the evening her kinsfolk and friends brought her body to the charnel ground, with firewood,
dhpak1.7:12.4: oil, and other requisites, and said to the keeper of the charnel ground: “Burn this body.”
dhpak1.7:12.5: And paying the keeper the usual fee, they turned the body over to her and departed.
dhpak1.7:12.6: When the keeper of the charnel ground removed the woman’s dress and beheld her beautiful golden-hued body, she straightaway thought to herself:
dhpak1.7:12.7: “This corpse is a suitable subject of meditation to show to the venerable.”
dhpak1.7:12.8: So she went to the elder, worshipped him, and said: “I have a remarkably good subject of meditation; pray look at it, venerable Sir.”
dhpak1.7:13.1: “Very well,” said the elder. So he went and caused the dress [28.187] which covered the corpse to be removed,
dhpak1.7:13.2: and surveyed the body from the soles of the feet to the tips of the hair.
dhpak1.7:13.3: Then he said: {1.71} “Throw this beautiful golden-hued body into the fire, and so soon as the tongues of fire have laid hold of it, please tell me.”
dhpak1.7:13.4: So saying, he went to his own place and sat down.
dhpak1.7:14.1: The keeper of the charnel ground did as she was told and went and informed the elder.
dhpak1.7:14.2: The elder came and surveyed the body.
dhpak1.7:14.3: Where the flames had touched the flesh, the color of her body was like that of a mottled cow;
dhpak1.7:14.4: the feet stuck out and hung down; the hands were curled back; the forehead was without skin. The elder thought to himself:
dhpak1.7:14.5: “This body, which but now caused those who looked thereon to forget the sacred word, has but now attained decay, has but now attained death.”
dhpak1.7:14.6: And going to his night-quarters, he sat down, discerning clearly decay and death.
dhpak1.7:15.1: Things are surely impermanent, their nature to arise, decay,
dhpak1.7:15.2: after arising do they cease, the mastery of them is good.
dhpak1.7:16.1: Awakening Having recited this verse, Mahā Kāḷa developed spiritual insight and attained Arahatship,
dhpak1.7:17.1: When Mahā Kāḷa attained Arahatship, the Teacher, surrounded by the assembly of bhikkhus,
dhpak1.7:17.2: traveling from place to place, arrived at Setavya and entered the Siṁsāpa forest.
dhpak1.7:17.3: Culla Kāḷa’s wives, hearing that the Teacher had arrived, thought to themselves:
dhpak1.7:17.5: So they sent and invited the Teacher.
dhpak1.7:17.6: Now when a visit is expected from the Buddhas, it is customary to prepare a seat in a place which is not circumscribed,
dhpak1.7:17.7: and in order to ensure that this shall be done, it is customary for a single bhikkhu to go in advance and give warning.
dhpak1.7:17.8: For the seat of the Buddhas must be set in the midst, {1.72} on the right of the Buddha must be placed the seat of the Elder Sāriputta,
dhpak1.7:17.9: on his left that of the Elder Mahā Moggallāna, and next to these on both sides must be arranged the seats for the assembly of bhikkhus.
dhpak1.7:17.10: Therefore the Elder Mahā Kāḷa, standing in the place where the bowls and robes were kept, sent forth Culla Kāḷa, saying:
dhpak1.7:17.11: “You go in advance and give warning to arrange the seats.”
dhpak1.7:18.1: From the moment the members of the household caught sight of Culla Kāḷa, they made a jest of him,
dhpak1.7:18.2: putting the low seats at the ends [28.188] where the elders of the assembly were to sit, and the high seats where the novices were to sit.
dhpak1.7:18.3: Culla Kāḷa said to them: “Do not arrange the seats thus;
dhpak1.7:18.4: do not put the low seats above and the high seats below.”
dhpak1.7:18.5: But the women, pretending not to hear him, said: “What are you doing here, walking about?
dhpak1.7:18.6: What right have you to give orders about the arrangement of the seats?
dhpak1.7:18.7: By whose leave did you go forth? Who gave you the going forth? What made you come here?”
dhpak1.7:19.1: And having thus made a mockery of him, they tore off his under and upper garments,
dhpak1.7:19.2: clothed him with white garments instead, placed a garland on his head, and packed him off, saying:
dhpak1.7:19.3: “Go fetch the Teacher; we will arrange the seats.”
dhpak1.7:19.4: Now those who have been bhikkhus but a short time, and have returned to the world before keeping a single Rains Retreat, are without a sense of shame.
dhpak1.7:19.5: Therefore Culla Kāḷa, free from any anxiety on the score of his clothing, went to the Teacher,
dhpak1.7:19.6: worshipped him, and taking with him the assembly of bhikkhus presided over by the Buddha, returned.
dhpak1.7:20.1: When the assembly of bhikkhus had finished their meal, Mahā Kāḷa’s wives thought to themselves:
dhpak1.7:20.2: “Culla Kāḷa’s wives recovered their husband; let us also recover ours.”
dhpak1.7:20.3: {1.73} Accordingly they invited the Teacher for the following day.
dhpak1.7:20.4: But on this occasion a different bhikkhu came to arrange the seats, and so Mahā Kāḷa’s wives failed of an opportunity to embarrass him.
dhpak1.7:20.5: When they had seated the Saṅgha presided over by the Buddha, they presented them with food.
dhpak1.7:20.6: Now Culla Kāḷa had two wives, Majjhima Kāḷa had four, and Mahā Kāḷa had eight.
dhpak1.7:21.1: Those of the bhikkhus who desired to eat sat down and ate their meal; those who desired to go out arose and went out.
dhpak1.7:21.2: The Teacher sat down and ate his meal. When he had finished his meal, those women said to him:
dhpak1.7:21.3: “Venerable Sir, Mahā Kāḷa will pronounce the formula of thanksgiving and then return; you go on ahead.”
dhpak1.7:21.4: The Teacher said: “Very well,” and went on ahead.
dhpak1.7:22.1: When the Teacher reached the village gate, the assembly of bhikkhus were offended and said: “What a thing for the Teacher to do!
dhpak1.7:22.2: Did he do it wittingly or unwittingly? Yesterday Culla Kāḷa came in advance, and that was the end of his monastic life.
dhpak1.7:22.3: But today a different bhikkhu came in advance, and nothing of the sort happened.”
dhpak1.7:22.4: The Teacher sent Mahā Kāḷa back and continued on his way.
dhpak1.7:22.5: The bhikkhus said: “The bhikkhu Mahā Kāḷa is virtuous and upright.
dhpak1.7:22.6: Will they put an end to his monastic life?” [28.189]
dhpak1.7:23.1: Hearing their words, the Teacher stopped and asked them: “What is it you are saying, bhikkhus?”
dhpak1.7:23.2: When they told him, he said: “But, bhikkhus, you do not think that Mahā Kāḷa is like Culla Kāḷa?”
dhpak1.7:23.3: – “Yes, venerable Sir; Culla Kāḷa has two wives, but Mahā Kāḷa has eight.
dhpak1.7:23.4: If his eight wives gather about him and seize him, what can he do, venerable Sir?” The Teacher said: “Bhikkhus, do not speak thus.
dhpak1.7:23.5: Culla Kāḷa lives a busy and active life and allows his thoughts to dwell on many pleasing objects.
dhpak1.7:23.6: My son {1.74} Mahā Kāḷa, on the other hand, does not live looking for pleasure, but is immovable, like a mountain of solid rock.”
dhpak1.7:23.7: So saying, he pronounced the following verses:
dhpak1.7:24.1: 7. Subhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ, indriyesu asaṁvutaṁ, bhojanamhi amattaññuṁ,
dhpak1.7:24.2: kusītaṁ hīnavīriyaṁ – taṁ ve pasahati Māro vāto rukkhaṁ va dubbalaṁ.
dhpak1.7:25.1: Contemplating what is pleasant, with sense faculties uncontrolled, not knowing the limit in food,
dhpak1.7:25.2: indolent, low in energy – Māra surely o’erthrows that one, like wind overthrows a weak tree.
dhpak1.7:26.1: 8. Asubhānupassiṁ viharantaṁ, indriyesu susaṁvutaṁ, bhojanamhi ca mattaññuṁ,
dhpak1.7:26.2: saddhaṁ āraddhavīriyaṁ – taṁ ve nappasahati Māro vāto selaṁ va pabbataṁ.
dhpak1.7:27.1: Contemplating the unpleasant, with their sense faculties controlled,
dhpak1.7:27.2: and knowing the limit in food, faithful, with energy aroused – Māra does not o’erthrow that one,
dhpak1.7:27.3: just as wind does not overthrow a mountain made of solid rock. {1.77}
dhpak1.7:28.1: Mahā Kāḷa’s former wives surrounded him and said to him: “By whose leave did you go forth?
dhpak1.7:28.2: Will you now become a householder?”
dhpak1.7:28.3: Having said this and much more to the same effect, they sought to strip him of his yellow robes.
dhpak1.7:28.4: But the elder, understanding their intention,
dhpak1.7:28.5: rose from the seat where he had been sitting and flew upwards by his supernatural power, rending the peak of the house asunder.
dhpak1.7:28.6: And having soared through the air, he descended to the ground as the Teacher spoke the concluding words of the verses,
dhpak1.7:28.7: praising the golden body of the Teacher and paying obeisance at the feet of the Realised One.
dhpak1.7:29.1: At the conclusion of the verse the assembled bhikkhus
dhpak1.7:29.2: were established in the fruition of Stream-entry.
